explanation.text:
SECOND SPEECH OF ELIPHAZ. (Job 15:1-35)

a wise man--which Job claims to be.

vain knowledge--Hebrew, "windy knowledge"; literally, "of wind" (Job 8:2). In Ecc 1:14, Hebrew, "to catch wind," expresses to strive for what is vain.

east wind--stronger than the previous "wind," for in that region the east wind is the most destructive of winds (Isa 27:8). Thus here,--empty violence.

belly--the inward parts, the breast (Pro 18:8).

headings.title: Eliphaz: Job Does Not Fear God

bsb.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

1.interlinear: Then answered/H6030 Eliphaz/H464 the Temanite/H8489 and said/H559

explanation.text:
Should a wise man utter vain knowledge,.... As Job had been thought to be, or as he himself thought he was, which he might say sarcastically; or as he really was, not worldly wise, nor merely wise in things natural, but in things divine; being one that had the fear of God, which is the beginning of wisdom, and wisdom itself; believed in Christ, and walked wisely and circumspectly before men; now it is not becoming such a man to utter vain knowledge, or such knowledge as is like the wind, or, as the Targum, windy knowledge; empty, not solid, nor satisfying, but swells and puffs up, and is knowledge falsely so called; but it does not appear that Job did utter such vain and fruitless things as deserved to be compared to the wind:

and fill his belly with the east wind; which is noisy and blusterous, rapid and forcible, bearing all before it, and very infectious in hot countries; and such notions Job, according to Eliphaz, satisfied himself with, and endeavoured to insinuate them into others; which were nothing but great swelling words of vanity, and tended to subvert the faith of men, and overthrow all religion, and were very unwholesome, infectious, and ruinous to the minds of men, as suggested.

bsb.text: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?

2.interlinear: Should a wise man/H2450 utter/H6030 vain/H7307 knowledge/H1847 and fill/H4390 his belly/H990 with the east wind/H6921

explanation.text:
Should he reason with unprofitable talk?.... That is, the wise man, such a man as Job; does it become him to talk such idle stuff? that which is false, and foolish, and frothy, that does not minister grace to the hearer, and is not for the use of edifying; as whatever is untrue, unwise, vain, and empty, must be useless and answer no good end; nothing is profitable but what tends to increase solid wisdom and spiritual knowledge, and to exercise grace, and influence an holy life; wherefore what are profitable to the souls of men are the doctrines of the word of God, and the experiences of the grace of God, communicated by his people one to another; and nothing but these, or what agrees with them, should come out of the mouth of a wise and good man; nor can such an one expect to convince men of their errors, or reprove them for their sins with success, who deals in words of no profit:

or with speeches wherewith he can do no good? but may do a great deal of hurt both to himself and others; but the same thing is here signified in different words,

bsb.text: Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?

3.interlinear: Should he reason/H3198 with unprofitable/H5532 talk/H1697 or with speeches/H4405 wherewith he can do no good/H3276

explanation.text:
fear--reverence for God (Job 4:6; Psa 2:11).

prayer--meditation, in Psa 104:34; so devotion. If thy views were right, reasons Eliphaz, that God disregards the afflictions of the righteous and makes the wicked to prosper, all devotion would be at an end.

bsb.text: But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.

explanation.text: The sophistry of thine own speeches proves thy guilt.

bsb.text: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

5.interlinear: For thy mouth/H6310 uttereth/H502 thine iniquity/H5771 and thou choosest/H977 the tongue/H3956 of the crafty/H6175

6.interlinear: Thine own mouth/H6310 condemneth/H7561 thee and not I yea thine own lips/H8193 testify/H6030 against thee

explanation.text: That is, Art thou wisdom personified? Wisdom existed before the hills; that is, the eternal Son of God (Pro 8:25; Psa 90:2). Wast thou in existence before Adam? The farther back one existed, the nearer he was to the Eternal Wisdom.

bsb.text: Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

7.interlinear: *Art thou the first/H7223 man/H120 *that was born/H3205 or wast thou made/H2342 before/H6440 the hills/H1389

explanation.text:
secret--rather, "Wast thou a listener in the secret council of God?" The Hebrew means properly the cushions of a divan on which counsellors in the East usually sit. God's servants are admitted to God's secrets (Psa 25:14; Gen 18:17; Joh 15:15).

restrain--Rather, didst thou take away, or borrow, thence (namely, from the divine secret council) thy wisdom? Eliphaz in this (Job 15:8-9) retorts Job's words upon himself (Job 12:2-3; Job 13:2).

bsb.text: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?

8.interlinear: Hast thou heard/H8085 the secret/H5475 of God/H433 and dost thou restrain/H1639 wisdom/H2451 to thyself

explanation.text: in us--or, "with us," Hebraism for "we are aware of."

bsb.text: What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?

9.interlinear: What knowest/H3045 thou that we know/H3045 not *what understandest/H995 thou which *is not in us

explanation.text: On our side, thinking with us are the aged. Job had admitted that wisdom is with them (Job 12:12). Eliphaz seems to have been himself older than Job; perhaps the other two were also (Job 32:6). Job, in Job 30:1, does not refer to his three friends; it therefore forms no objection. The Arabs are proud of fulness of years.

bsb.text: Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side—men much older than your father.

10.interlinear: With us *are both the grayheaded/H7867 and very aged/H3453 men much/H3524 elder/H3117 than thy father/H1

explanation.text:
consolations--namely, the revelation which Eliphaz had stated as a consolatory reproof to Job, and which he repeats in Job 15:14.

secret--Hast thou some secret wisdom and source of consolation, which makes thee disregard those suggested by me? (Job 15:8). Rather, from a different Hebrew root, Is the word of kindness or gentleness addressed by me treated by thee as valueless? [UMBREIT].

bsb.text: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?

11.interlinear: *Are the consolations/H8575 of God/H410 small/H4592 with thee is there any secret/H328 thing/H1697 with thee

bsb.text: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,

12.interlinear: Why doth thine heart/H3820 carry thee away/H3947 and what do thy eyes/H5869 wink at/H7335

explanation.text: That is, frettest against God and lettest fall rash words.

bsb.text: so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?

13.interlinear: That thou turnest/H7725 thy spirit/H7307 against God/H410 and lettest *such words/H4405 go out/H3318 of thy mouth/H6310

explanation.text: Eliphaz repeats the revelation (Job 4:17) in substance, but using Job's own words (see on Job 14:1, on "born of a woman") to strike him with his own weapons.

explanation.text:
Repeated from Job 4:18; "servants" there are "saints" here; namely, holy angels.

explanation.text:
filthy--in Arabic "sour" (Psa 14:3; Psa 53:3), corrupted from his original purity.

bsb.text: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?

16.interlinear: How much more abominable/H8581 and filthy/H444 *is man/H376 which drinketh/H8354 iniquity/H5766 like water/H4325

explanation.text: In direct contradiction of Job's position (Job 12:6, etc.), that the lot of the wicked was the most prosperous here, Eliphaz appeals (1) to his own experience, (2) to the wisdom of the ancients.

bsb.text: Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen,

explanation.text: Rather, "and which as handed down from their fathers, they have not concealed."

18.interlinear: Which wise/H2450 men have told/H5046 from their fathers/H1 and have not hid/H3582 *it

explanation.text: Eliphaz speaks like a genuine Arab when he boasts that his ancestors had ever possessed the land unmixed with foreigners [UMBREIT]. His words are intended to oppose Job's (Job 9:24); "the earth" in their case was not "given into the hand of the wicked." He refers to the division of the earth by divine appointment (Gen 10:5; Gen 25:32). Also he may insinuate that Job's sentiments had been corrupted from original purity by his vicinity to the Sabeans and Chaldeans [ROSENMULLER].

bsb.text: to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.

19.interlinear: Unto whom alone the earth/H776 was given/H5414 and no stranger/H2114 passed/H5674 among/H8432 them

explanation.text:
travaileth--rather, "trembleth of himself," though there is no real danger [UMBREIT].

and the number of his years, etc.--This gives the reason why the wicked man trembles continually; namely, because he knows not the moment when his life must end.

bsb.text: A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.

20.interlinear: The wicked/H7563 man travaileth/H2342 with pain all *his days/H3117 and the number/H4557 of years/H8141 is hidden/H6845 to the oppressor/H6184

explanation.text: An evil conscience conceives alarm at every sudden sound, though it be in a time of peace ("prosperity"), when there is no real danger (Lev 26:36; Pro 28:1; Kg2 7:6).

bsb.text: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.

21.interlinear: A dreadful/H6343 sound/H6963 *is in his ears/H241 in prosperity/H7965 the destroyer/H7703 shall come/H935 upon him

explanation.text:
darkness--namely, danger or calamity. Glancing at Job, who despaired of restoration: in contrast to good men when in darkness (Mic 7:8-9).

waited for of--that is, He is destined for the sword [GESENIUS]. Rather (in the night of danger), "he looks anxiously towards the sword," as if every sword was drawn against him [UMBREIT].

bsb.text: He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.

22.interlinear: He believeth/H539 not that he shall return/H7725 out of darkness/H2822 and he is waited/H6822 for of the sword/H2719

explanation.text:
Wandereth in anxious search for bread. Famine in Old Testament depicts sore need (Isa 5:13). Contrast the pious man's lot (Job 5:20-22).

bsb.text: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.

explanation.text: stretcheth . . . hand--wielding the spear, as a bold rebel against God (Job 9:4; Isa 27:4).

on his neck--rather, "with outstretched neck," namely, that of the rebel [UMBREIT] (Psa 75:5).

explanation.text:
The well-nourished body of the rebel is the sign of his prosperity.

explanation.text:
The class of wicked here described is that of robbers who plunder "cities," and seize on the houses of the banished citizens (Isa 13:20). Eliphaz chooses this class because Job had chosen the same (Job 12:6).

bsb.text: he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.

Rather, he shall not increase his riches; he has reached his highest point; his prosperity shall not continue.

explanation.text:

bsb.text: He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.

Rather, "let him not trust in vanity or he will be deceived," etc.

Literally, "it (the tree to which he is compared, Job 15:30, or else his life) shall not be filled up in its time"; that is, "he shall be ended before his time."

explanation.text: Images of incompleteness. The loss of the unripe grapes is poetically made the vine tree's own act, in order to express more pointedly that the sinner's ruin is the fruit of his own conduct (Isa 3:11; Jer 6:19).

bsb.text: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.

explanation.text:
Rather, The binding together of the hypocrites (wicked) shall be fruitless [UMBREIT].

explanation.text:
Bitter irony, illustrating the "unfruitfulness" (Job 15:34) of the wicked. Their conceptions and birthgivings consist solely in mischief, etc. (Isa 33:11).
